questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Be prepared to stop if the light is flashing.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: A yellow sign with a traffic signal picture warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to respond to it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead makes a sharp turn. Slow down and prepare for an abrupt change in direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign alerts you that a side road will intersect ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of an upcoming curve in the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop and wait until it is safe to proceed through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check for traffic coming from both directions before proceeding.
Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you wish to enter or cross.
Maintain a steady speed and check for traffic coming from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you wish to enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop so that other vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians can pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You will see this sign at intersections where U-turns would be unsafe due to traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
A right turn is permitted on a green arrow only.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Some warning signs have a bright yellow-green background. These signs alert you to upcoming conditions, including sharp curves and turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Do not enter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with two-way traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Travel in the direction of the arrow.
Look for a destination sign to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Travel in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a lane control sign. You must move your vehicle in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs indicate work zones. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Follow their directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guards signals for you to go.
Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Be alert and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed at this location. Regulatory signs like this must be obeyed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and yield to traffic on the main road when merging.
Always come to a complete stop.
Activate your turn signal and proceed into traffic at the usual speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to traffic on the main road when merging.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means you must wait for traffic on the other road to pass before you proceed. You do not need to stop completely if no vehicles are coming, but you should slow down and enter the intersection carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Be ready to merge with traffic entering your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to merge with traffic entering your lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that traffic will be merging into your lane from the right. Be prepared to allow them to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the right lane is closing ahead. You need to merge left safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked line or before the crosswalk. Stop before the intersection if you cannot see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
You must not travel below the speed indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign shows the maximum speed allowed on this road. You can drive slower if conditions require it, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that pedestrians cross at this location. Be alert and let people cross safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turning on a red signal is prohibited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning on a red signal is prohibited.
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign means you cannot turn right or left when the light is red at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an intersection ahead. Be ready for traffic or to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. Slow down because it takes longer to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A triangular red and white sign means you must let other traffic go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand signals because they don't have turn signals. A left arm straight out means the cyclist is turning left.
